threads.thread_goal: Align on current journey map, key gaps, and overall pathway design.

messages.text: I have uploaded a first pass at the current client journey map for the Integrated Employment Readiness Pathway project_title, based on 12 recent cases and our notes from T1. It is sitting alongside the draft pathway overview in A1. The map runs from referral through assessment, stabilisation, skills building, placement, and in-work support. Can you all take a look and sanity-check whether the stages and handovers reflect what actually happens on the ground before we lock anything in?

Thanks for pulling this together. Looking at the current journey, I notice we do not explicitly show a pause between crisis stabilisation and any employment-focused work. In practice, that pause can be weeks. I wonder if we should make that a distinct stage in A1 so we do not rush people into workshops before they are ready.

I have gone through the map as well. From the employment support side, I think the skills building and placement prep bits are a bit merged. For example, CV support and confidence building groups happen before we even talk about specific employers. Maybe we should split that into two stages so T3 later can align more clearly with the pathway.

From the moves side, the current map shows relocation only once, just before placement. In reality, we sometimes support a move earlier, for example when someone needs to leave unsafe housing before they can even think about work. Should we add an optional relocation step that can appear either before stabilisation or before placement, so T5 and A5 later do not feel bolted on?

Looking at the early stages, I do not see a clear health and wellbeing screening point. For the pilot, I would suggest we place a short screening step right after initial holistic assessment, so T4 and A4 can feed into planning before any move or workshop is offered.

Agree on both the stabilisation pause and the split between skills building and placement prep. How about we define the new pathway stages as: 1) referral and triage, 2) holistic assessment and consent, 3) stabilisation and wellbeing, 4) pre-employment skills building, 5) placement preparation and matching, 6) relocation and first days in work, 7) in-work support and review, 8) exit and follow-up. Relocation would be an optional step that can occur either between 3 and 4 or between 5 and 6, as suggested.

On the pre-employment skills building stage, would that be where the workshops from T3 sit, or is that more one-to-one work? I am just trying to picture how many sessions we would expect clients to attend before we talk to employers.

I was thinking T3 would mostly live in that pre-employment skills building stage, with maybe one shorter session in the placement prep stage focused on rights at work and what to expect. For number of sessions, maybe 3 core ones, but we can confirm that in the workshop thread.

The eight stages you listed make sense to me and reflect what I see in case notes. One thing I would add is a clear handover from assessment to health screening, and from skills building to placement prep, so T6 and A3 can spell out who leads at each point. Otherwise we risk the same coordination gaps we have now.

Yes, especially between assessment and health screening. For example, if the assessment flags mobility issues, I need that information before any move is booked or workshop venue is chosen. Could we make it explicit in A3 that the health screening summary is part of the standard handover notes at that point?

From my side, I would really value a simple case summary that includes any health flags and safeguarding notes before we plan a move. If A3 and later A5 can reference that shared summary, it will reduce the back and forth on the day of the move.

I will update A1 and the draft for T6 so that each of the eight stages has a named lead role and a standard handover note, including a short case summary. For now, can we confirm that these eight stages are the backbone of the new pathway for the pilot, so we can align T2, T3, T4, T5, and T6 against them?

I am happy to treat those eight stages as the main structure for the pilot. We can still tweak wording, but the flow feels right and should help us explain the pathway clearly to partners and clients.

Agreed on the eight stages. From the gaps you highlighted in T1, the ones I see most often are: 1) people waiting a long time between assessment and any meaningful activity, 2) confusion about who is doing what when several workers are involved, and 3) clients not understanding what the pathway offers. Are those the right top three to focus on in the pilot?

I would support those three. I would just phrase the first one as delays between assessment and stabilisation or skills building, because sometimes health or housing work needs to happen before any employment activity. If we shorten that delay and make the steps clearer, it should also reduce anxiety for clients.

On confusion about who is doing what, I see that a lot around moves and first days in work. Clients often think I will solve things that actually sit with housing or the employer. If T6 and A3 can make those boundaries clearer, that would directly address that gap.
On clients not understanding the pathway, would that be mainly solved through the information pack in T7 and A8, or do we also need something visual in A1 that we can show them in first meetings?

To close this out, can we agree that the top three gaps we will prioritise in the pilot design are: 1) long and unclear waits between assessment and the next meaningful step, 2) lack of clear coordination and handovers between roles, and 3) clients not having a simple explanation of the pathway and what to expect. These will drive how we shape A1, T2, T3, T6, and T7.

Yes, I am comfortable naming those three as our priority gaps for the pilot. They are also the ones most likely to affect engagement and safeguarding, so focusing there should give us the biggest impact within the 21-day setup window.

threads.thread_goal: Finalise assessment, health screening, and safeguarding tools.

messages.text: I have uploaded a draft holistic assessment and employment readiness template for T2, plus a first version of the consent and privacy section that could become A2. It follows the eight pathway stages we agreed and includes social, health, skills, and employment goals. Can you review with a focus on what is realistic to complete in a first or second meeting?

I have also added a draft health and wellbeing screening checklist for T4, which could sit as A4. It is intentionally short: a few questions on physical health, mental health, medication, mobility, and any current treatment. I tried to align it with our existing organisational health protocols so we do not create a parallel system.

I like the structure of the assessment template. One concern is that the risk and safeguarding section might be a bit light for the client group we are targeting. For example, there is only one question on domestic abuse and none on exploitation at work. Could we expand that section slightly and then make sure it links clearly into the safeguarding flow in A7 and T9?

I had a look at the employment goals part. Some of the questions might be a bit abstract for people with low literacy or who have been out of work for a long time. Maybe we can add some simple examples or use more everyday language, so it lines up better with how we will talk in the workshops from T3.

I agree. For example, instead of asking about long-term career goals, we could ask what kind of work they might like to try first, or what kind of tasks they feel comfortable doing. That might give us enough to start without overwhelming them.

On A4, I suggest we add a simple prompt about sensory needs and communication preferences, as that will affect workshop accessibility and any move planning. It can be a tick-box with space for notes, so it does not slow us down too much.

From a safeguarding angle, it would help me if the health screening summary clearly flags any mobility or cognitive issues that might affect a move or first commute. Maybe A4 could have a short section that is automatically pulled into the shared case summary we mentioned in A3.

Good point on the safeguarding questions. I will expand that section to include prompts on domestic abuse, financial exploitation, and any concerns about coercion around work. I will also add a clear instruction that any red flags there should trigger the safeguarding and incident flow in A7 and T9, rather than being handled informally.

That sounds right. We should also make sure the consent section in A2 is very clear about what information is shared with whom, especially between social work, health, and movers. Could we add a simple table that explains this in plain language, so clients can make an informed choice?

On the health side, I will adjust A4 so that any safeguarding concerns picked up during screening also point directly into A7 and T9. That way, whether the concern is raised in assessment or screening, it ends up in the same reporting flow.

For T9, I have drafted a simple safeguarding and incident reporting flow that could become A7. It defines incident types, thresholds, and timelines, and it shows when movers should escalate concerns rather than trying to manage them alone. I would appreciate a check from both social work and health to ensure it matches organisational policy.

I have reviewed the draft A7. The overall flow looks sound and aligns with our safeguarding policy, but we should add a step that ensures the client is informed about what is happening, where it is safe to do so. Also, we might want to clarify who is responsible for updating the case record after an incident.

From a health perspective, I am comfortable with the thresholds and timelines in A7. The only addition I would suggest is a reminder to check for any immediate health risks when an incident is reported, and to involve clinical services if needed.

I have now incorporated the feedback into T2 and A2: simplified employment questions, expanded safeguarding prompts, and a clearer consent table. Unless there are any strong objections, I suggest we treat this version of the holistic assessment and consent checklist as the one we will use in the pilot, with only minor wording tweaks if needed.
I am happy to go ahead with the current T2 and A2 for the pilot. They are comprehensive but still usable in practice, and they link clearly into the safeguarding and health tools.

I have finalised A4 based on the comments: added sensory and communication prompts, and explicit links to A7 and T9 when there are safeguarding concerns. It should now be ready to integrate into the pathway and the shared case summary.

I have updated A7 and T9 to include the step about informing the client where safe, and to state that the lead social worker is responsible for updating the case record after an incident. With those changes, can we confirm that this safeguarding and incident reporting flow is the one we will use across roles in the pilot?
Yes, with those clarifications I am comfortable adopting A7 and T9 as our standard safeguarding and incident flow for the pilot.

threads.thread_goal: Shape the workshop programme and client-facing information pack.

messages.text: I have drafted an outline for the employment readiness workshops for T3: three core sessions plus an optional fourth. They cover 1) understanding the pathway and rights, 2) strengths and skills, 3) preparing for work and placements, and 4) optional peer support. I tried to keep activities simple and adaptable for mixed literacy. The draft is in the shared folder.

I have started a first version of the client-facing information pack for T7, which could become A8. It explains the eight stages of the pathway, what clients can expect, and their rights and consent. It is quite text-heavy at the moment, so I would welcome ideas on how to make it more accessible.

Looking at the workshop outline, I like that session one starts with understanding the pathway and rights. It might help to mirror the structure of A1 and A8 so that clients see the same stages in different formats. Could we use a simple visual timeline in that session, matching the eight stages we agreed?

On the information pack, I suggest we keep the main leaflet very short and plain, and then link to more detailed information if needed. For example, one page on what the pathway is, one on rights and consent, and one on who is involved. We can then use A8 as the base and adapt it for different literacy levels.

For session two on strengths and skills, could we include a short piece on managing health at work and reasonable adjustments? That would help clients think about what they might need to stay well in a placement, and it links nicely to what we pick up in A4.

In session three on preparing for work and placements, it might be useful to include something on practical logistics: travel to work, what happens on the first day, and how moves are handled. That way, when we use A5 and T5 in practice, clients already have a sense of what to expect.
Good idea on the visual timeline. I can add a simple eight-stage diagram to session one that matches A1 and A8, and build an activity where clients place example scenarios along that timeline.

I can rework A8 into a shorter leaflet as you suggest: three pages max, with simple headings and icons. I might need some help checking that the wording on rights and consent matches what we have in A2 and A7.

Happy to review the rights and consent wording once you have a new draft of A8. If you base it on the consent table in A2 and the key steps in A7, we should be able to keep it consistent and still accessible.

I will add a short section in session two on managing health at work and reasonable adjustments, and maybe a simple role-play where clients practice explaining a support need to a supervisor. I will keep it light so it does not feel like a clinical session.

I can provide a short checklist of what usually happens on move day and first commute, based on A5 and T5, so you can turn that into an activity in session three. That might help reduce anxiety for clients who have had bad experiences with moves before.

Looking across the four sessions, I wonder if we are trying to do too much in the optional peer support session. Maybe we keep the core structure as three required sessions for the pilot, and treat the fourth as something we can test with a small group if capacity allows.

I agree. For the pilot, it would be safer to lock in three core sessions and treat any peer support activity as an add-on rather than a formal requirement. That will also make scheduling easier within the 21-day window.

Ok, I will reframe T3 so that the workshop programme for the pilot is three core sessions: 1) pathway and rights, 2) strengths, skills, and health at work, 3) preparing for placements, logistics, and first days. Peer support will be an optional add-on we can test informally.
That structure works for me and lines up well with the pathway stages and our constraints. I am happy to treat those three sessions as the locked structure for the pilot workshops.

I have now shortened A8 to a three-page leaflet with icons and a simple timeline. It covers what the pathway is, what clients can expect, and their rights and consent. I have tried to mirror the wording in A2 and A7 as much as possible, but would appreciate a final check from social work.

I have reviewed the latest A8. The rights and consent sections are consistent with A2 and A7, and the language feels accessible. I suggest we sign this off for use in the pilot, with the understanding that we can tweak it after we get client feedback.
Agreed, the current A8 is good enough to go live for the pilot. We will build in a quick feedback question in the workshops so we can refine it later.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on logistics for moves, workplace transitions, and employer engagement.

messages.text: I have uploaded a draft safe relocation and workplace transition checklist for T5, which could become A5. It covers planning the move, protecting dignity and belongings, first commute, and first day at work. I have also noted where we need information from social work and health before we confirm dates.

On the employer side, I have started T11 and have a list of four community employers who are open to placements. They are mostly in retail and cleaning. I have had initial conversations about expectations and support needs, but I still need to confirm details with two of them.

I can help follow up with one of the employers if that would speed things up. Maybe we should also think about having at least one placement that is less physically demanding, for clients with mobility issues flagged in A4.

Looking at A5, it would help if the checklist explicitly asked whether any health or mobility issues from A4 require adjustments to the move or commute, such as extra time, equipment, or a quieter time of day. That way we do not rely on memory.

From a safeguarding perspective, I would like A5 to include a quick check on whether the new accommodation and workplace are safe and appropriate, especially for clients leaving abusive situations. We should also make sure the safeguarding flow in A7 and T9 is referenced if any concerns arise during a move.

On the employer list for T11, do we have at least one employer who is used to working with people who have been out of work for a long time or who have fluctuating health? That might make the first placements smoother while we test the pathway.

One of the retail employers has some experience with supported placements, and there is a small charity shop that has taken volunteers with health issues before. I can prioritise confirming those two, plus one of the cleaning employers who seemed open to adjustments.

I will update A5 so that the first section asks explicitly whether there are any health or mobility issues from A4 that affect the move or commute, and what adjustments are needed. I will also add a prompt to check with the client about preferred times and any sensory needs.
That will make a real difference. It also means we can use the same information from A4 across workshops, moves, and placements, rather than asking clients the same questions several times.

I support adding those safety checks into A5. We should also make sure that if a mover or employment worker spots a concern about the workplace, they know to use A7 and T9 rather than trying to negotiate alone with the employer.

Help with follow-up would be great. I can share the notes from my initial calls so you can pick up with the charity shop. We can then aim to have at least three employers confirmed for T11 by the end of tomorrow.
Ok, I will contact the charity shop this afternoon and check their expectations and support needs. I will add notes to the T11 document so we have a clear profile for each employer.

I have now updated A5 to include safety checks on new accommodation and workplaces, and explicit references to A7 and T9 if any concerns arise. With these changes, I think the checklist is ready to use in the pilot, but I would like a quick safeguarding review from social work before we call it final.

I have reviewed the latest A5. The safeguarding elements and links to A7 and T9 look appropriate, and the dignity and belongings section is clear. I am comfortable approving this checklist for use in the pilot.
Agreed, A5 as it stands is fit for purpose for the pilot. We can capture any learning from early moves in the incident and feedback processes.

Quick update on T11: we now have verbal interest from the retail employer, the charity shop, and one cleaning company. All three understand that clients may have health or support needs and are open to reasonable adjustments. I will write up a short profile for each, including typical tasks and supervision style.

That gives us a good starting mix of employers. Unless anyone has strong concerns, I suggest we confirm these three as our initial pilot partners, with the option to add more later if capacity allows.
I am happy to go ahead with those three employers for the pilot. They give us some variety while still being manageable in terms of coordination.

threads.thread_goal: Set up tracking, evaluation, and team rituals for the pilot.

messages.text: I have created a first draft of the pilot outcome and attendance tracking sheet for T8, which could become A6. It tracks workshop attendance, key pathway milestones, and whether someone moves into a placement or job. I have used pseudonymised client IDs rather than names.

Thanks for setting that up. I have also drafted an evaluation plan for T12, outlining key questions, success indicators, and when we will review progress. It suggests a mid-pilot review around week three and an end-of-pilot review after placements have run for a bit.

Looking at A6, I think we should make sure we track not just outcomes but also any safeguarding incidents and wellbeing concerns, even if they are resolved quickly. That will help us see if the new pathway is reducing or increasing risk.

From a health perspective, it would be useful if A6 could capture a simple wellbeing rating at key points, for example after assessment, after workshops, and after the first week in placement. Nothing too detailed, just enough to see trends.

For employment outcomes, should we distinguish between short placements, longer placements, and sustained jobs in A6? That might help us show progress even if people do not move straight into permanent work.
Could we also log in A6 whether a move or first commute was completed as planned, and whether any issues came up? That would give us some data on how well A5 and T5 are working in practice.

I can add columns in A6 for safeguarding incidents and wellbeing ratings, plus a simple code for move or commute issues. I will keep the sheet as simple as possible so it does not become a burden to update.

In the T12 evaluation plan, I have proposed a small set of key indicators: engagement (attendance at workshops and appointments), progression (movement through pathway stages), safety and wellbeing (incidents and ratings), and employment outcomes (placements and jobs). Are there any other indicators people feel are essential for the pilot?

Those indicators cover the main areas I would expect. We might also want to capture a simple staff feedback rating on how usable the new tools are, but that could sit in the evaluation survey rather than A6.
I agree with the proposed indicators. For wellbeing, it might be enough to use a simple three-point scale (better, same, worse) at key points, so staff do not have to remember numbers.
For moves, a simple yes or no on whether the move or commute went as planned, plus a short note if not, should be enough. We can then use A7 and T9 for any incidents that meet the threshold.

I have now updated A6 to distinguish between short placements, longer placements, and sustained jobs, and added the wellbeing and incident fields we discussed. I will share a short note on how to fill it in so we are consistent.

Given the discussion, can we confirm that for the pilot we will track: 1) engagement (attendance at workshops and key appointments), 2) progression through pathway stages, 3) wellbeing trends, 4) safeguarding incidents and move issues, and 5) employment outcomes (placements and jobs). These will be our core indicators in A6 and T12.
Yes, I am comfortable naming those as our key indicators for the pilot. They should give us enough information to judge whether the pathway is working without overloading staff.

On team rituals, T12 suggests a weekly 30-minute virtual checkpoint to review A6 and any incidents, plus a short async standup twice a week in this channel. For the standup, each role would post what they did for the pilot yesterday, what they plan today, and any blockers.
The weekly checkpoint and twice-weekly async standup sound manageable to me. It would help if we fix the days and times now so people can plan around them.
I can usually make a short virtual checkpoint on Tuesday afternoons. For the async standup, maybe Monday and Thursday mornings would work, so we catch issues early in the week and before the weekend.
Tuesday afternoon works for me as well, and I can post async updates from the van if needed. Having fixed days will also help me plan moves around the checkpoint where possible.

Based on availability, I propose we set the weekly virtual checkpoint for Tuesdays at 15:00, and the async standups for Monday and Thursday mornings, to be posted by 11:00. We can adjust if this clashes with shifts, but it gives us a starting rhythm.
Those timings work for me, and they fit around most frontline commitments. Let us go with that cadence and review after the first two weeks if needed.
